questions.q: Juan Hervas served as the 'Arquitecto Municipal' (City Architect) of Manila in the late 1880s. Which major civic building in Intramuros, which served as the seat of the City Council, is among his most famous designs?
questions.n: Hervas designed the 1884 version of this building, known for its grand marble staircase and Neo-Renaissance elegance.

questions.q: Hervas was the lead architect for the original terminal of the Manila Railroad Company. What is this building known as today?
questions.n: The original brick structures of Tutuban were designed by Hervas in 1892, showcasing 19th-century industrial-influenced architecture.

questions.q: Which of these European revival styles was Juan Hervas most known for bringing to the commercial and civic streets of Manila?
questions.n: Hervas utilized these classical European revivals to give Manila's 19th-century buildings a sophisticated, 'Old World' character.

questions.q: Hervas designed several prominent commercial buildings along which famous street, known as the financial heart of old Manila?
questions.n: Hervas helped define the high-end European look of Escolta during its 19th-century peak.

questions.q: True or False: Unlike many later Filipino architects who studied in the US, Juan Hervas received his architectural training and orientation from Europe (Spain).
questions.n: As a late Spanish-era architect, his education and stylistic influences were strictly European.

questions.q: The 'Ayuntamiento de Manila' in Intramuros was often called the 'Marble Palace.' Aside from being the seat of the City Council, what was its primary architectural style as designed by Hervas?
questions.n: Hervas used the grand symmetry and classical motifs of the Renaissance revival to project the authority and wealth of the Spanish city government.

questions.q: Which of these materials was most commonly used in the 'lower' floor of Hervas's buildings, following the 'Bahay na Bato' tradition of the time?
questions.n: Following Spanish building codes for earthquake safety, the ground floor was built with heavy masonry to support the wooden upper floor.

questions.q: Juan Hervas was the 'Arquitecto Municipal' of Manila. What was the primary responsibility of this position?
o: Designing and supervising the construction of public works and civic buildings
questions.n: As the City Architect, he was in charge of the official look and structural integrity of Manila's government buildings.

questions.q: Hervas worked on the 'Manila-Dagupan Railway' terminus. Why was the use of brick in Tutuban Station significant at the time?
o: It reflected the industrial and utilitarian style of 19th-century European train stations
Because it was cheaper than using wood
Because brick was a brand new invention in the 1890s
It was meant to make the building look like a church
questions.n: The brickwork gave the station a durable, modern, and European look suitable for the country's first major rail line.

questions.q: Before Juan Hervas, most large buildings in the Philippines were designed by 'Maestros de Obra.' What made Hervas different?
o: He was an academic architect with formal training from Europe
He did not know how to draw
questions.n: Unlike master builders who learned through apprenticeship, Hervas brought formal, scholarly architectural principles to Manila.

questions.q: Hervas's 'Ayuntamiento' was located in which district, known as the 'Walled City'?
questions.n: As the seat of the Spanish government, Intramuros housed the Ayuntamiento and other major civic buildings.

questions.q: True or False: Juan Hervas arrived in the Philippines during a period of economic boom and urban modernization in the late 19th century.
questions.n: The opening of the Suez Canal and the growth of trade created the demand for the sophisticated buildings Hervas designed.

questions.q: What happened to most of Juan Hervas's architectural works in Manila?
o: They are all perfectly preserved and open to the public
They were all turned into modern skyscrapers
Many were destroyed during the Battle of Manila in 1945
questions.n: Like much of Manila's Spanish heritage, his buildings suffered immense damage during World War II.

questions.q: The 'Marble Palace' (Ayuntamiento) featured a grand staircase. This emphasis on grand entryways is a hallmark of which European influence?
questions.n: European civic architecture used grand staircases to create a sense of arrival and to reflect the dignity of the institution.

questions.q: Juan Hervas helped design Escolta to look like a European high street. Which of these functions was Escolta best known for?
questions.n: Known as the 'Queen of Manila Streets,' it was the center of luxury trade and finance where Hervas's designs flourished.
